The Story of Money

A Have you ever paid for something with a shell? People have used salt, cows and small white cowrie shells as money. Before money, people often swapped things — a bag of grain for a pair of shoes. But what can you do if the shoemaker doesn't want grain?

B The first coins appeared more than 2,600 years ago in Lydia, a kingdom in what is now western Turkey. They were made of electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver. Coins were easy to carry and easy to count, and the idea soon spread to other countries.

C Paper money came much later. In 1024 the government in China began to print official paper notes. In the 13th century the Italian traveller Marco Polo was amazed that people in China bought and sold things with pieces of paper. Europe's first banknotes were printed in Sweden in 1661 — partly because Swedish copper coins were so big that one of them could weigh nearly 20 kilograms.

D In 1950 the Diners Club in New York made the first card that people could use in many different restaurants — a cardboard one. According to a famous story, the founder, Frank McNamara, had the idea when he forgot his wallet at dinner — but years later, the man who wrote the company's advertising said that he had made the story more exciting. On 27 June 1967 the world's first cash machine opened outside a bank in north London. It gave people £10 at a time.

E Today, millions of people never carry cash at all. In a 2025 survey by Sweden's central bank, only 5 per cent of people said that they paid in cash the last time they bought something in a shop. In 2023 the number was 10 per cent.

F Uzbekistan introduced its own money, the som, on 1 July 1994. Money has changed many times since the first coins, but one thing hasn't: it only works when people trust it.

Grammar · present perfect or past simple

TUSHUNTIRISH — PRESENT PERFECT YOKI PAST SIMPLE

A Present Perfect (have / has + uchinchi shakl) — hozirgacha boʻlgan hayotingizdagi tajriba, qachonligi aytilmaydi: I've used a cash machine. · She has never borrowed money. · Have you ever bought anything online? · I've worked on sales days three times before.

B Past Simple — tugagan vaqt, qachon ekanini aytamiz yoki soʻraymiz: I bought it yesterday / last week / in 2024 / two days ago / when I was ten. · When did you buy it?

C Suhbat koʻpincha Present Perfect bilan boshlanib, Past Simple da davom etadi: Have you ever lost your wallet? — Yes, I have. — Where did you lose it? — I lost it on the bus. Yana: the cleverest customer I've ever met.

D Istisnolar. Tugagan vaqt bilan Present Perfect hech qachon ishlatilmaydi: I bought it yesterday — I've bought it yesterday emas. been yoki gone? She's been to Dubai (borib, qaytib keldi) · She's gone to Dubai (hozir oʻsha yerda).

MODEL — AN OPINION TEXT

Is it better to shop online or in a shop?

In my opinion, it is better to shop in a real shop, for two reasons.

Firstly, you can see and touch things before you buy them. For example, I have bought clothes online three times, and twice they were the wrong size. Secondly, you can ask a shop assistant for help, and sometimes you can get a discount. Last week my father got 10 per cent off a fridge because he asked.

To sum up, online shopping is fast, but a shop is better for important things.
